newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-NIGERIAN COACH UNDER FIRE AFTER GUINEA DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIAN COACH UNDER FIRE AFTER GUINEA DEFEAT.

text.p: Frenchman Phillipe Troussier is weathering heavy criticism less than three months after coaching Nigeria into the World Cup finals.
"This team certainly should be overhauled," said sports minister Jim Nwobodo after Nigeria lost their final qualifying match to Guinea at the weekend.
"The players were not match-fit and they lacked commitment and concentration."
Troussier has already crossed swords with officials since signing from Ivory Coast club ASEC Mimosas, where he was dubbed the 'White Wizard'.
He has subsequently accused Nigerian soccer authorities of failing to respect his contract.
"I signed a 17-month contract in March with a clause to re-negotiate after qualifying for the World Cup," said Troussier, who claims to have been offered the coaching post with Burkina Faso.
"If they can't respect their own side of the deal, no problem."
"I'm ready to quit if the NFA (Nigerian Football Association) don't cooperate with me. I will not go on my knees to beg for the position of Nigeria's trainer at France '98."
Local newspaper reports have suggested that the Frenchman first planned to move on last month when the NFA accused him of going to Morocco on holiday without permission.
